notes: Run with the skill-creator skill against a scratch copy of the project (config/ is modified). Every scenario must end with `python -m hub.validate_config` showing no new ERROR.

evals.name: modbus-modicon-meter
evals.prompt: Add an energy meter at site kish, area gate, IP 192.168.10.31, unit 1. Registers: 30001 Voltage L1 float32 V, 30007 Current L1 float32 A, 30053 Total active power float32 W, 33204 Active energy int64 Wh. Low word first.
evals.expected_output: config/devices/meter_02.yaml (next free counter) with input registers at addresses 0, 6, 52, 3203, word_order little, units kept as given (W, Wh), validator OK.
expectations: Addresses are converted from Modicon notation: 0, 6, 52 and 3203, all register_type input
energy tag uses data_type int64 (not skipped, not uint32)
word_order is little and byte_order is left at the default
Units are W and Wh exactly as stated, not converted to kW/kWh
No tag is read_write
The validator is run and the report table lists all four tags

evals.name: mqtt-payload-with-timestamp
evals.prompt: سنسور دما و رطوبت روی تاپیک kish/gate/th-01/data این رو می‌فرسته: {"ts":1767225600,"data":{"t":24.6,"h":51},"bat":87}
evals.expected_output: An mqtt device on plant_broker with telemetry_topic kish/gate/th-01/data, timestamp_path $.ts / timestamp_format unix_s, tags temperature (float32 degC), humidity (float32 %), battery_level (integer %), reply in Persian.
expectations: telemetry_topic is exactly kish/gate/th-01/data
timestamp_path is $.ts and timestamp_format is unix_s; ts is not a tag
humidity is float32 even though the sample value 51 is whole
battery level is an integer type
device_id follows the repo pattern (env_sensor_NN) and th-01 is kept in the description
The reply to the user is in Persian; file contents are English
Inferred units are marked as inferred

evals.name: drive-status-bits-behind-gateway
evals.prompt: Add the ABB ACS580 pump drive. It's on RS-485 behind the Moxa MGate at 192.168.10.40 port 502, slave address 5. From the manual: holding register 40001 = status word (bit 0 ready, bit 1 running, bit 3 fault), 40102 = output frequency, 0.01 Hz per count, unsigned.
evals.expected_output: A modbus_tcp device with host 192.168.10.40, unit_id 5, a uint16 status_word at holding 0, bool tags with bit 0/1/3 on holding 0, output_frequency uint16 at holding 101 with scale 0.01 Hz; gateway mentioned in description.
expectations: unit_id is 5 and host is the gateway address
Status flags are bool tags with register_type holding, address 0 and bit 0, 1 and 3
Bit tags are read-only
output_frequency has scale 0.01 and unit Hz
The description names the Moxa gateway
The report warns that bit numbering (0 = LSB) should be checked against a live state

evals.name: collision-is-asked-not-dodged
evals.prompt: Add a power meter at 192.168.10.21 unit 1, registers 30001 voltage float32 V.
evals.expected_output: The skill notices that meter_01 already uses 192.168.10.21:502 unit 1 and asks whether this is a re-add or a typo, citing meter_01's area and map; it does not change the IP or unit id on its own.
expectations: The collision with meter_01 is detected before writing
The user is asked (or, if unattended, the file is written with enabled: false and a TODO)
host and unit_id are not altered to avoid the collision

evals.name: missing-info-no-invention
evals.prompt: Add the Siemens S7-1200 in the pump station. I don't have the register list yet, IP is 192.168.10.60.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains that the S7-1200 Modbus map comes from the MB_SERVER block and asks for it from the PLC programmer; it asks for the unit id; it does not invent registers. If it writes a file, it has no tags and lists TODOs.
expectations: No register address is invented
The answer mentions MB_SERVER / the PLC programmer as the source of the map
Missing values are asked for in one message

evals.name: out-of-scope-sparkplug
evals.prompt: Add our Ignition gateway; it publishes Sparkplug B on spBv1.0/kish/#.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains Sparkplug B is binary protobuf and not supported by the mqtt JSON driver; suggests OPC UA from Ignition instead; writes no mqtt device.
expectations: No mqtt device file is written for the Sparkplug topic
OPC UA is offered as the supported path

evals.name: bulk-excel
evals.prompt: Import the devices in this workbook.
evals.expected_output: scripts/excel_to_devices.py is used with --dry-run then --check; 5 devices (meter_03, vfd_01, gate_counter_01, env_sensor_03, plc_02); vfd_01 is written disabled with host todo.invalid; meter_03.frequency is skipped as TODO; the report lists TODOs and writable tags from the script output.
expectations: The script is run (not hand-written YAML)
--dry-run runs before the real import
meter_03 relay is a coil at address 0 (the text-typed 00001) and demand_limit is holding 100 with scale 0.1
vfd_01 is enabled: false with host todo.invalid
Both writable meter_03 tags are listed as warnings in the report
The final validator run has no ERROR
